title: Kind tables
description: The kind tables of Lathe's schema, one per kind with typed columns and its parent columns as foreign keys, and the part and link tables beside them, in the numbered migrations: a requirement's statement, a test's file and a component's file are columns. The domain table's comment says what a domain is.

title: Modeling skill
description: The plugin's `model-a-domain` skill, which an agent follows to write a domain model. Its first step finds the product's business capabilities and makes each one a domain, with the questions that tell a capability from a layer.

title: Kinds in the schema
description: meta_kind and meta_kind_parent: every kind with its label, stage, folder, obligation and ID convention, and its parent kinds nearest first with the column that names each. Each kind's migration adds its rows: a domain rule may sit under an entity, an aggregate or a domain, and a layer under a layer or a domain.

title: Relations in the schema
description: A link table per relation, its ends foreign keys to a kind or a supertype, with each relation's role, labels and description and its allowed pairs, each pair once. The `supports` pairs, from a test to each obligation kind, have no role, so coverage and the proof checks never read them.

title: Product configuration
description: `loadConfig(root)` reads `lathe.config.json`, whose one setting is `data`, the data folder, refuses any other setting by name, and finds the installed package's own folder, which holds the schema and Lathe's check rows.

title: Product kind tables
description: Generates a product's own kinds and relations from its declarations: a table per product kind with its fields, joined to the obligation supertype when it is one, and a link table per new product relation or a pair added to one of Lathe's. It refuses a kind named like one of Lathe's tables, a parent or an end that is no kind, and a field named like a column every record has.

title: Product declaration tables
description: product_kind, product_kind_field and product_relation: each kind declared once by its name, each field once by its place, each relation pair once, every one with its description, and both labels required on a relation; a kind's folder is a foreign key into the schema's folders.

title: Capability table
description: The capability table: each under a domain, its position a whole number from 1 and unique in its domain, so the store refuses a repeated or broken one; use cases, flows and tests sit under a capability or the domain.

title: Use case outside capability check
description: The `use-case-outside-capability` check row: a warning for each use case whose parent is a domain that has at least one capability.

title: Pattern setting table
description: pattern_setting rows: each setting of a pattern in order, its name lower-case letters, digits and underscores starting with a letter and unique in its pattern; the store refuses another.

title: Capability and use case kinds
description: The capability kind under a domain with its required position, and the use_case kind, with flow and test, allowed under a domain or a capability.

title: Follows relation
description: The `follows` link table, from a domain or a use case to a pattern, with no role: following a pattern is neither design nor proof. A follower's setting_value rows hang on its follows link.

title: Record placement
description: The record_parent and record_scope views every database of the store has: a record's parent is the first of its parent columns with a value, and its product and domain are found by walking parents, so a record under a capability, a layer or an entity takes its ancestors' domain with no special case.

title: Pattern rule table
description: pattern_rule rows: the setting a rule depends on and its applies-when setting are foreign keys into its pattern's settings, and an applies-when condition is given whole or not at all.

title: Flow step table
description: The flow_step kind under a flow, with a required position and path, each position once per path of its flow, and in 010-links.sql the `fulfills` and `uses` pairs a step may start.

title: Step order check
description: The `step-order` check row, for the steps of a flow and of a technical flow alike: a path whose positions do not run 1, 2, 3 without a gap, reported once on the first step after the first gap and naming every missing number, with paths compared trimmed and in any letter case. Its messages name the step and its flow by their kinds' labels.

title: Flow step fulfills outside flow check
description: The `flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow` check row: compares each step's `fulfills` targets with its flow's reach (requirements of the use cases it carries out, the rules they apply, the rules of the patterns they or the domain follow, and interaction requirements fulfilling any of these or under the flow). Steps of a flow that carries out nothing are skipped.

title: Flow fulfills differs from steps check
description: The `flow-fulfills-differs-from-steps` check row: a flow with at least one step whose own `fulfills` target no step of it fulfills.

title: Pattern settings asked only of patterns with settings
description: The `pattern-setting-missing` check row asks only for the settings a pattern has, so a pattern with no settings asks nothing, and a domain that follows a pattern is never asked.

title: Pattern and pattern rule kinds
description: The pattern kind under a product with no required columns, its settings as pattern_setting rows, and the pattern_rule kind, a proof-only obligation.

title: Folders in the meta-model loader
description: `readRecords` in the engine reads each kind's folder from the schema description, and the schema's folders into `Workspace.sections`, the stages' folders by position and then the product-level ones.

title: Folders in the schema
description: meta_section rows: each folder with its stage, position, label and description. A kind's section, and a product kind's, is a foreign key into it, so the store refuses an unknown folder.

title: Section stage mismatch check
description: The `section-stage-mismatch` check row: each kind whose folder has a stage other than the kind's own; a folder with no stage is never compared.

title: Layer kind in the meta-model
description: The layer kind in the Technical specification folder, under a domain or a layer, with a required whole-number position and not an obligation; component and design_flow sit under a layer or a domain, and no other kind names a layer as its parent.

title: Layer order check
description: The `layer-order` check row: each layer whose position another layer with the same parent also has, naming the parent and the other layers.

title: Component outside layer check
description: The `component-outside-layer` check row: each component whose parent is a domain that has at least one layer.

title: Layer-blind coverage
description: The coverage views read a design link's source domain from record_scope, never from its parent, so a component in a layer designs and builds in its domain, including the pattern rules that domain owes.

title: Entity kind and relations in the schema
description: The entity kind in the define stage's domain model folder under an aggregate, its role root or child, its fields as entity_field rows each with a required name, meaning and type; and in 010-links.sql the has_one, has_many and refers_to link tables from entity to entity and involves from domain rule to aggregate. The domain_rule table says a rule across aggregates names them with involves.

title: Parts in the workspace loader
description: `readRecords` in the engine gives each record its part rows, such as an entity's entity_field rows and an event's event_field rows, in key order, under the record that owns them.

title: Aggregate root validation
description: The aggregate-root validation query, run in every load and write: an aggregate with entities and no root, or more than one, is refused, naming how many roots it has.

title: Entity fields check
description: The `entity-fields` check row: an entity or a domain event that lists no fields, named as an entity or as an event.

title: Parts inside their aggregate check
description: The `has-crosses-aggregate` check row: each `has_one` or `has_many` whose target entity sits in another aggregate than its source; `refers_to` links are never read.

title: Unreached child entity check
description: The `entity-unreferenced` check row: walks `has_one` and `has_many` links inside each aggregate from its one root, and reports each child entity the walk does not reach.

title: Reference model and Markdown
description: The `Reference` shape (kinds, tables, relations, folders and checks) and `renderReference`, which writes it as one Markdown document: how data is kept, then each kind with its table, the other tables, and each relation, folder and check under its own anchor (`kind-use_case`, `table-entity_field`, `relation-proves`, `folder-test-plan`, `check-unproved`), with links between them. It documents the engine's own problem, `data-refused`, as a check.

title: Reference loader
description: `buildReference(root)` opens the product's store and builds the reference from its schema description, product kinds included, and the check rows that run: Lathe's in position order, the engine's own, then the product's. It reads no records.

title: Committed reference
description: Lathe's reference, as the reference script writes it, committed so agents can read it without running anything. `npm --prefix lathe run reference`, and the package build, regenerate it.

title: Reference script
description: Writes the reference of a product, Lathe's by default, as Markdown into `lathe/REFERENCE.md`, prints it with `--print`, or writes it to the file `--out` names. `npm --prefix lathe run reference` runs it.

title: Reference API
description: `GET /api/reference` answers with the product's `Reference` as JSON, for `lathe serve`, the desktop app and the app's Vite dev server alike.

title: Domain event kind and relations in the schema
description: The domain_event kind in the define stage's domain model folder under an aggregate, its fields as event_field rows; and in 010-links.sql the raised_by link table to an entity and reacts_to from an aggregate, a use case or a component.

title: Event unheard check
description: The `event-unheard` check row: a warning for each domain event that no `reacts_to` link targets, from any record, saying this can be fine and naming what might react.

title: Event tense check
description: The `event-tense` check row: a warning for each domain event whose title has no past form as its last word or after its first: a word of four or more letters ending in "-ed", other than a short list of words that are not past forms, or one of the irregular past forms its query lists.

title: Raised by outside aggregate check
description: The `raised-by-outside-aggregate` check row: each `raised_by` whose target entity sits in another aggregate than the event.

title: Domain named for technology check
description: The `domain-named-for-technology` check row: a warning for each domain whose title, or whose code after the product prefix, holds a technology word as a whole word, saying which word it found where. The words are listed in its query.

title: Domain rule involves check
description: The `domain-rule-involves` check row: a warning for each domain rule under a domain that involves fewer than two aggregates, for each aggregate of another domain such a rule involves, and for each rule under an aggregate or an entity that uses `involves`.

title: Format reference pages
description: The format page, a kind's page and a check's page, each in the workbench: one pane with the title in it, and the side bar with the facts beside it (a bottom sheet on a phone). The format page says how records are kept, then shows the index of kinds by stage and folder, the relations and the checks by severity; a kind's page shows its columns, and a check's page its query. Kinds and checks are clickable rows.

title: Format reference data
description: Builds the reference from the loaded data: the schema description and the check rows from `GET /api/spec`; a check a problem names that has no row is the engine's own, listed without an explanation. Holds the format pages' addresses and the lookups the pages share: a kind's relations in and out, the checks that name it, its folder.

title: Links to the format reference
description: Every problem list shows its check code as a link to the check's page, and the Checks page titles each group with one. A record's facts link its Kind row to the kind's page and its column labels to the column there; a group's facts link its kind.

title: Kinds and checks in quick find
description: Quick find's items include each kind as "Kind: <label>" and each check as "Check: <name>" (the reference's checks, fetched once something is typed, and any check a problem names), ranked like every other item.

title: Record format command
description: The keymap's `goFormat` command is titled "Record format" in the palette (g then f), and the shortcuts sheet links the record format; the nav no longer does.

title: Record actions
description: Checks a page's record action (`parseRecordRequest`), finds the data file whose row starts with the record's ID (`findDataFile`, with `DataFiles` reading the folder again when a row moves), and builds the native right-click menu (`recordMenuTemplate`). The main process reveals the file with `shell.showItemInFolder` and copies the ID with the clipboard.

title: Editor choice
description: The editor Open in editor uses, kept in `settings.json` in the user data folder (`parseSettings`), and how to open a file in it (`editorLaunch`): a known editor by its bundle ID on macOS (`open -b`) or its command elsewhere, the system's default app, or a custom command run in a login shell with the file as an argument.

title: Desktop record hooks
description: The app's desktop-only hooks, mounted with the title bar: `DesktopRecordActions` in a record's facts (three ghost buttons), the right-click listener that finds the record under a graph node, a record link or the page title (`recordIdAt`) and asks for the native menu, and the error count sent for the Dock badge. Each shows or listens only when `window.latheDesktop` has the member it needs.

title: Standard kinds and meets relation in the meta-model
description: The standard and standard_rule kinds in the Shared folder right after the patterns, not obligations, and in 010-links.sql the meets link table from a component, a technical step or a test, with no role.

title: Standard rule unmet check
description: The `standard-rule-unmet` check row: a warning for each standard rule that no `meets` link targets, naming the link to add.

title: Standard page
description: A standard's Rules section: a table of its rules in ID order, one body per group headed by its name, each with the records that meet it, read from `meets` links and labeled by the relation's reverse label, or "Nothing yet". `RecordContent` shows it on a standard's page in place of the children list. A rule's own page needs nothing of its own: Traceability lists its incoming links under Met by, and the nav lists standards because their kinds sit in the Shared folder.

title: Standards in the graph key
description: The graph key's Design entry names a standard and its rules, its shapes name them beside the pattern and pattern rule, its ruler mark says what it tells apart, and its design line names `meets`; `relationStyle` in `GraphPage.tsx` draws a `meets` link in the design line style.

title: API, integration and technical flow kinds
description: The api and integration kinds in Interaction design under a domain, endpoint under an API or a domain, and interaction_requirement under a view, an endpoint, a flow, an API, an integration or the domain. The design_flow and design_step kinds, with a step's required position and path, are in 008-technical-specification.sql.

title: Technical flow relations
description: The `deepens` link table from a technical flow to a flow, `uses` from a technical step to a component, and `satisfies` from a technical step to a requirement, domain rule, interaction requirement or pattern rule, with the `design` role, so coverage and `unsatisfied` count it as design without asking more of either.

title: Technical flow deepens nothing check
description: The `design-flow-deepens-nothing` check row: a warning for each technical flow with no `deepens` link.

title: Design skill
description: The plugin's `design-the-domain` skill, which an agent follows to write a domain's design: its table of design kinds, and its sections on APIs and integrations and on technical flows, with the columns and links each takes, written through the MCP tools.

title: Store loading
description: `openStore` reads every data file, with Lathe's check rows beside it, and loads them into a fresh database of the schema in one transaction, a self-referencing table level by level, then runs the validation queries; a row it refuses is a problem naming the file, line and rule. Before the database sees a row it refuses an unknown table or column, a value of the wrong type, an empty text, a missing required column, a key twice in a file and an ID used twice across kinds.

title: Data file form
description: How a row becomes a line and back: `normalizeRow` types each value by its column, `sortRows` orders rows by key, and `rowLine` and `tableText` write one JSON object per line, columns in the table's order, empty columns left out, UTF-8 with a trailing newline, so a change to a row is a one-line diff.

title: Schema description
description: `readMigrations` and `applyMigrations` apply the numbered migrations in order and record them; `describeSchema` reads every table, column, type, enum, key, foreign key, check and comment back from DuckDB, with the meta rows: kinds with their parents and positions, relations with their pairs, supertypes and folders.

title: Validation queries
description: The link view and the validation queries each load and write runs in its transaction, for what DuckDB cannot hold as a constraint because it spans tables: relation-pair, link-crosses-product, aggregate-root and product-kind-product.

title: Merge driver
description: `mergeData` and `mergeDataFiles` merge a data file's base, ours and theirs row by row by key: a row added, changed or removed on one side is taken, a row both sides added alike is kept once, and a key added twice with different content or a row changed on both sides is a clash. The merged rows are sorted and checked against the table's own rules. `lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P` writes the merge over ours and exits 1 on a clash.

title: Row types
description: The row type of every stored table, generated from the schema by `npm --prefix lathe run schema` (`lathe/scripts/schema-types.ts`); a test fails until it is regenerated after a migration.

title: Data commands on the command line
description: `lathe add`, `set`, `move`, `link`, `unlink`, `remove`, `show`, `list` and `next-id`: flags and help generated from the schema description, each write one call to the command layer, a refusal printed with every reason and an exit code of 1, and `--json` for the result as JSON.

title: Data operations
description: The data operations the command line and the MCP tools share: each command's input checked against the schema description and turned into store commands, and the reads (show, list and next-id) answered the same way for both.

title: MCP server
description: `lathe mcp`: the data commands and `check` as MCP tools over stdio, their input schemas generated from the schema description, product kinds included; a refusal is returned with its reasons, and the tool list is announced again when the schema changes.

title: MCP launcher
description: Starts the repo's own `lathe mcp` for the project folder the plugin runs in, found by `plugin/scripts/lathe-root.mjs`, and says why it cannot start outside a Lathe repo.

title: Field names folded
description: Unique indexes on an entity's and an event's field names, trimmed and in any letter case, so the store refuses a field named like another of the same record but for spacing or case.

title: Kind order
description: meta_kind.position: the place of each of Lathe's kinds in the order people read kinds, from the product and its domains to open questions; a product's own kinds have none and follow by name.

title: Command line
description: The `lathe` command: `check` calls `loadWorkspace` on the product repo and prints the report (errors, warnings, then a coverage line per domain and obligation kind with designed, built, proved and planned counts, and the tests by state), or the whole workspace with `--json`, and sets the exit status; data the store refuses is reported as `data-refused` errors. `init` writes the product's config and its product row through the store. In this repo, `npm --prefix lathe run check` runs `check` on the repo root.

title: Lathe's checks
description: Lathe's check rows, one check each, in position order. Errors: `entity-fields`, `has-crosses-aggregate`, `layer-order`, `pattern-setting-missing`, `proof-not-in-file`, `raised-by-outside-aggregate`, `section-stage-mismatch`, `step-order`, `test-file-missing` (an error or, for a planned test, a warning) and `test-file-missing-id`. Warnings: `unsatisfied`, `unproved`, `use-case-without-requirements`, `component-file-missing`, `pattern-not-followed`, `obligation-outside-domain`, `rule-not-applied`, `use-case-without-flow`, `interaction-requirement-fulfills-nothing`, `test-type-mismatch`, `component-satisfies-nothing`, `test-proves-nothing`, `use-case-outside-capability` and the other structure, entity, event, flow and proof warnings. What the schema enforces (IDs, parents, required columns, links, enums, positions) is not a check: the store refuses it.

title: Rule not applied check
description: The `rule-not-applied` check row: a warning for a domain rule that no use case links to with `applies`.

title: Use case without flow check
description: The `use-case-without-flow` check row: a warning for a use case that no flow `carries_out`, in a domain (by `record_scope`) that has a flow.

title: Interaction requirement fulfills nothing check
description: The `interaction-requirement-fulfills-nothing` check row: a warning for an interaction requirement with no `fulfills` link.

title: Test type mismatch check
description: The `test-type-mismatch` check row: a warning for a `domain_rule` test proving only requirements, or an `acceptance` test proving only domain rules, naming the IDs it proves.

title: Product relation key
description: The primary key of `product_relation` (name, source kind and target kind): a relation pair declared twice is refused by the store as `primary-key`, naming the file and line.

title: Link end refusals
description: The store's foreign-key diagnosis: a link whose target is not in the table its relation's end points at, such as a supertype, is refused once, naming the kinds that end accepts (`names no implements_target (endpoint, view)`).

title: Unique ID and parent refusals
description: The store refuses a row whose ID another record has once, as `unique-id`, naming that record's file and line; a parent column naming no record once, as a foreign key naming the missing record and its kind; and a column the kind does not have as `column`. Data it refuses is not checked further, so one mistake is one problem.

title: Config settings
description: `loadConfig` accepts only the `data` key of `lathe.config.json` and refuses any other, `checks` included, as an unknown setting naming it.

title: Check runner
description: `runChecks` in the engine: runs the check rows in order (`orderChecks`: Lathe's by position, then each product's), each query on one of a few connections side by side, and keeps their problems in run order. A row's problems take its name and severity, or the severity each row returns for `error_or_warning`; a product's check keeps only problems about records of its product; a query that fails is one error saying the check could not run. The file facts and coverage views are filled before it runs.

title: Too many children check
description: The `too-many-children` check row: counts each record's children by kind from `record_parent`, leaving out tests, a flow's or technical flow's steps per path and requirements, interaction requirements, pattern rules and standard rules per group, and reports each count over the product's `product_setting.max_children` (15 when it has no row).

title: Lone child check
description: The `lone-child` check row: counts each capability's and layer's own children, of every kind, and each group's members, and reports each that has exactly one, naming the child (and, for a group, reporting it on the group's parent).

title: max_children in product_setting
description: The `product_setting` table: one row per product, whose `max_children` is a whole number of at least 1 by its CHECK; the store refuses any other value. A product without a row takes the default, 15 (`DEFAULT_MAX_CHILDREN`).

title: max_children in the checks
description: `too-many-children` reads `max_children` from the product's `product_setting` row, and 15 when it has none, as any product check may read it.

title: Checks in the reference
description: `referenceOf` reads each check row's summary, explanation, severity and kinds into the reference, and `orderChecks` lists them as they run: Lathe's by position, the engine's own `data-refused`, then each product's.

title: Component satisfies nothing check
description: The `component-satisfies-nothing` check row: a warning for a component with no `design` link (such as `satisfies`).

title: Test proves nothing check
description: The `test-proves-nothing` check row: a warning for a test with no `proof` link (such as `proves`) and no `supports` link.

title: Link crosses product validation
description: The `link-crosses-product` validation query, run in every load and every write: a link whose source sits in one product and whose target sits in another is refused, whatever its relation. Text is never read for IDs.

title: Refused data as problems
description: `loadWorkspace` turns a `StoreError` from opening the store into one `data-refused` error per refusal, its message from `formatProblem` (file, line and rule), and returns no records, links or coverage, so nothing is checked until the data loads.

title: Lathe's checks beside the product's
description: The store loads Lathe's own `lathe/data/check.jsonl` beside the product's data as read-only rows, so no product's write changes them, and refuses a product check row whose name one of Lathe's rows has, naming `lathe/data/check.jsonl`.

title: Check and problem tables
description: The `check` table: `name` (lower case with hyphens, the key), `product_id` (none for Lathe's), `position`, `severity` (error, warning or error_or_warning), `summary`, `explanation` and `query`, all required and non-empty, and `kinds`; and the `problem` result table (`check_name`, `severity`, `record`, `message`) that a run's problems are rows of.

title: Guard hook
description: A PreToolUse hook: reads the tool call on standard input and, when it writes a `.jsonl` file in a Lathe repo's data folder (found through `lathe-root.mjs`, the configured folder included), answers the permission decision deny with a reason pointing at Lathe's MCP tools; any other edit gets no output. It always exits 0.

title: Hook declaration
description: Declares the guard hook to Claude Code: a PreToolUse hook on Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit that runs `scripts/guard-data-files.mjs` from the plugin root.

title: Spec pages
description: The product, domain, record and checks pages, built from one fetched workspace. They read it; a record's changes go through its record actions (`LA-EXP-C86`). Every record ID is shown through one link component, and the fixture note is shown above every page.

title: Markdown rendering
description: Renders a record's text fields (or the reference's descriptions) from Markdown with `marked`, gives each heading an anchor, and sanitizes the HTML with `dompurify` before it reaches the page.

title: Graph model
description: Pure functions over the indexed workspace: the picture the camera frames around a record or group (its parent, and its descendants down to the depth), the Links switch's one hop of the center's own links, the column of each node in that picture by its depth in the tree (a cross-linked record one column after the record it was reached from, a tree position winning) and its row (by its parent's row, then the nav's order), the trace chain of a requirement or rule with its own columns by kind, the breadcrumb trail, the group nodes with marks summarizing their members, and the gaps and summary the side bar shows.

title: Graph sizes and a trace's layout
description: A trace box's size, 190 by 56 at text scale 1; `traceGrid`, which stacks a trace's columns of boxes in row order, each as tall as its wrapped label needs, centered on the center, since a trace is a chain and not part of the map; and `boxExit`, where a line leaves a box.

title: Graph page
description: The graph view over the one map (`LA-EXP-C64`), drawn on a canvas each frame by the painter (`LA-EXP-C80`) from each box's plate (`LA-EXP-C81`): record boxes in their stage's colors with error and gap badges, each kind drawn in its shape (`LA-EXP-DR65`, a domain a hexagon, `LA-EXP-DR61`), as its outline in the Tree view and a mark in the Nested and Voronoi views, folder-shaped groups, every drawn box with its label and bars where the level of detail asks for them (`LA-EXP-DR60`), level parent lines and dashed, curved cross-links with their words, the toolbar, filters, side bar, legend and minimap (a true overview of the map, `LA-EXP-UC03-R15`). The text measure the maps are laid out with is the canvas's, once the label's faces have loaded (`LA-EXP-C82`); each label is drawn in the lines its map broke it into, at the text scale it shares with its siblings, each line at its map size times the zoom (`LA-EXP-DR58`), so nothing is laid out again and text is crisp at any zoom. The camera (`LA-EXP-C49`) is the page's own: a new focus, depth or pane size glides it (`LA-EXP-DR59`); the wheel and a pinch zoom about the pointer, a drag pans, the zoom buttons zoom about the middle, and each move draws the next frame, every point placed relative to the camera's center. The pointer finds the box under it by the map's outlines (`LA-EXP-C84`), for the hover spotlight (fading on the shared motion), the tooltip, a click and a tap. A visually hidden layer of the drawn boxes, in the keyboard's order, carries focus, the arrow keys, Enter and Escape and each box's role and name; the focused box is drawn with the focus ring, and the layer takes what a glide passes over once as it starts. The Layout switch (`LA-EXP-UC03-R16`, the `graphLayout` command) draws the Nested map (`LA-EXP-C67`) and the Voronoi map (`LA-EXP-C68`, once the worker has laid it out) with the same camera, canvas, keyboard, spotlight, filters, minimap and side bar: a parent drawn before its children, no parent lines or bars, a cell drawn as its polygon, and Links between the cells' labels. The canvas's element offers a test hook, `graphScene`, with what it draws (each box's place on screen and in the map, its label lines with their fonts, its badges and states, the lines and the camera), and `graphHit`, its hit test.

title: Graph routes and entry points
description: The entry points to the graph: every record, group, product and domain page's Graph view (the nav has no Graph item), and where the older `/graph/<id>` addresses lead. Kept apart from the graph page so these load without the graph's canvas.

title: Domain page record lists
description: The domain page's lists, where each design group (flows, views, endpoints) nests its interaction requirements and the records of any other obligation kind under each record, as the define groups nest rules and requirements. Each test row carries its state tag, and a planned test's row is dimmed. The record page here is only chrome around the record content.

title: Record content
description: `RecordContent` takes the index, a record ID, an optional `onNavigate` and optional header actions, and shows the record: header, its typed fields and part rows (`RecordText`), problems, facts, parent, children (under their groups, when they name one) and links both ways. A test shows its state, with a note when it is planned; an interaction requirement shows where it sits and what it fulfills. It is a CSS container, so its two columns fold into one below about 760 pixels of its own width, as at half the screen beside the graph.

title: Long list
description: `LongList` takes items, a render function, a search-text function, a key function and a label. Up to 10 items it renders a plain list. Past 10 it adds a search box (Escape clears it), a live count, a "Nothing matches" status, and a focusable scrolling area whose height it measures from the first 10 rows, once and unfiltered, so filtering never makes it jump. Every list in the spec pages uses it, and it imports nothing from them, so the side bar uses it too.

title: Graph groups
description: The group functions in the graph model: which records have their children grouped, a group's ID (its place in the graph's tree; only the tree's groups are groups), members, plural label and summed marks, and the framed picture's walk through groups, a level each. A group is a level of the parent/child tree, so it takes the column after its parent and before its members, in the map as in the framed picture.

title: Graph group nodes and the hostable graph view
description: The folder-shaped group node with its name, count and marks; the side bar for a focused group; the legend entry. `GraphView` takes `focus`, `onNavigate` and `hrefFor`, so any pane can host it, and it frames the focus again whenever its container is resized.

title: Graph group addresses
description: Builds and reads a group's address, its place in the graph's tree, alongside `/<record-id>` for a record.

title: Focus addresses and views in the link
description: Builds every address of a record or group, by `addressOf`: a record's bare ID (`/<id>`, a product's and a domain's too) and a group's place in the graph's tree (`/<domain-id>/<stage>/<folder>`, `/<parent-id>/<kind>`); reads the `view` query parameter, by view names only; and says whether a stored page is a focus page's address (`isFocusPath`), so the tabs and the spaces drop any that is not.

title: Focus page: Wiki, Graph and Model panes
description: The page for one record, group, product or domain: its open views as panes side by side in the order Wiki, Graph, Model (Model only where it is offered), under one page bar (`app/src/views/PageBar.tsx`: the tab strip at its left; the View toggles, a divider and the side bar toggle at its right), each pane a panel with one slim header (its view's name; its Close when more than one pane is open and its full screen button, all icon buttons), the page title at the top of the leftmost pane (one fixed height above a graph or a model), the wiki pane (its scroll kept per tab), the graph pane (its settings kept per tab), the model pane, a resize handle in every gap with each pane's size a weight kept per tab, full screen for any pane, the view commands and the tab commands (keep, close, next and previous). On a phone (`PhoneLayout`) it shows one view at a time under the page bar, compact, with the side bar and the open pages as bottom sheets. `app/src/views/address.ts` reads and writes the open views in the address.

title: The side bar
description: The page's last column, as VS Code's secondary side bar: the switcher of Details, Outline and History at its top (a labeled group of `aria-pressed` icon buttons), the hide button, and the view shown under its own heading. It works out what Details describes from the node under the pointer or selected, which the graph, the Model view and the wiki's rows tell it through a small store (`app/src/views/sideBarState.ts`, so a hover redraws only the side bar), and keeps the view mode's open state and view per tab and as last used. Its styles are `app/src/views/SideBar.css`.

title: Side navigation
description: The nav: header with the logo and the collapse toggle, quick find, the Specs and Tools sections that fold on their own, products whose domain lists fold, the current page marked and scrolled into view, quiet badges, and a footer with Appearance and the source of the specs; the rail of icons when collapsed, and a full-screen sheet on a narrow screen that keeps Tab inside it. Every row is one full-width `NavRow`, as in VS Code's explorer: indented by padding for its depth with its indent guides inside it, its chevron at its start, the current page's row carrying the selection over the whole row, hover tinting the whole row, and a 1 px outline on the selected row while the nav is used from the keyboard; on a coarse pointer the rows are 44 px tall.

title: Quick find
description: A combobox that ranks every record, domain and product against what is typed (exact ID, ID prefix, title start, title word, anywhere) and opens the chosen one; arrow keys move, Enter opens, Escape clears.

title: Tree list (one level, folded)
description: Rows that each fold one level of nested rows under a disclosure button, with the nested count on the row, an Expand all / Collapse all ghost button, opened rows remembered for the session, a search that opens a row just for its match, Right and Left arrow keys as in a tree view, and page-wide expand and collapse for the command palette. It knows nothing about specs and uses the long list inside.

title: Record rows and record trees
description: `RecordRowBody` (a record's link, key fields, test state, followed pattern, coverage marks and problem badge) and `RecordTree` (records one level below the page's record, their own children folded under them, counted as "4 requirements"), used by the domain, record and group pages and the side bar.

title: The graph's part of the side bar's Details
description: What the drawn graph connects to the center (and how), the files a trace reaches, and the legend, as long lists, kept apart from the graph's canvas so the side bar loads without the graph. The side bar's Details shows it in the Graph view only.

title: Record links in rendered text
description: After a text field's Markdown is rendered and sanitized, walks its text (skipping code, pre and links) and replaces each whole ID token that names a record of the space, other than the record itself, with a link carrying the record's title; a code span holding one lone such ID is wrapped in the link. Any other ID-shaped token stays as written. A plain click on a link moves within the app, through the host's navigation when it has one.

title: A record's text with the records it names
description: `proseLinks` finds the IDs a text field names that are records of the space (never the record itself), with their titles, and `Prose` renders the field with them linked. It only changes how the text reads: an ID in text never enters the links, the graph or coverage.

title: Patterns in the graph
description: A pattern's rules are its children, so they sit one column to its right like any children, and a use case's `follows` link is a cross-link: a use case reached from the pattern by it sits one column after the pattern. Offers trace mode for a pattern rule. The graph page draws `follows` in its own pattern line style, named in the legend.

title: The nav without a Graph item
description: The side navigation and its rail list no Graph item; the graph is reached from each page's Graph view toggle, Ctrl+G or Alt+G, Ctrl+2 and the command palette.

title: Flow steps table
description: `FlowSteps` takes the index and a flow and, when the flow has steps, shows them as a table in order (`stepsOf`: by position, then ID), or a table per path when they sit on several (`pathsOf`: main first, then by name). Each row has a disclosure that unfolds the step's description and the titles and kinds of what it uses and carries out; the table has Expand all. A technical flow's steps read the same way, with the columns Component and Satisfies, and their transaction, locks and statements folded under each row. `RecordContent` shows it on a flow's and a technical flow's page.

title: Flow steps in the graph
description: A flow's steps are its children, so they hang one column right of the flow (through a group only when the flow has children of more than one kind, as for any record). In trace mode a fulfilling step sits in a column between the flows and the components, and brings its flow and the components it uses; a satisfying technical step sits just before the components, and brings its technical flow and the component it uses.

title: Spaces
description: `useSpaceState` works out the current space from the page (`productOfPath`) or the one last chosen, and remembers each space's last page in session storage; `spaceOf` gives a product's icon or monogram and color; `SpaceMark` draws it.

title: Space rail and scoped nav
description: The rail at the far left of the nav (the spaces, and nothing above every product), kept when the nav collapses and inside the narrow-screen nav sheet; beside it, from the space's own index, the current space's product page, domains folding into their Define and Design folders, groups, and Tools with the space's Checks and its counts.

title: Quick find in the space
description: `findItems` reads the current space's index, so only its records (and the format's kinds and checks) are found; `rankItems` ranks them as one list, walked by the arrow keys.

title: Space commands
description: Registers `switchSpace1` to `switchSpace9` for the spaces in rail order, each titled "Switch to <product>", and announces the switch.

title: Checks per space
description: The Checks page at `/<product-id>/checks` reads the space's own index: its product's problems by check, then the problems of no product under Workspace. The products page beside it lists each product with its name and domain count only.

title: Folder model
description: Places a product's and a domain's records in stages and folders from `Workspace.sections`, lifting a capability's records of other folders into theirs, and finds the nav rows that hold a record or a group.

title: Folders in the side nav
description: The current space's Shared folder, domains, stages and folders as foldable rows with counts, opened along the current page's branch and remembered for the session.

title: Folders on the domain page
description: The domain page's stages and folders as headings, each folder's records listed directly or under one heading per kind.

title: A group page's folder
description: The group page's eyebrow names the stage and folder of its kind.

title: Layer and test groups in the folder model
description: Gives each folder its groups: Technical specification by layer, each sub-layer a group within its layer, and Test plan by family and what each test proves (computed from its parent, `test_type`, `proves` and `supports` links, with no group level when only one group has tests), and finds the groups on a record's nav branch, through every layer above it.

title: Layer and test-group rows in the side nav
description: Draws a folder's groups as foldable rows with counts: a layer's row beside a link to its page, a test group's row a fold only, opened along the current page's branch.

title: Folder groups on wiki pages
description: Heads a folder's groups on the domain page and a test group page: a layer's title linking to its page, test groups as plain headings, each group's records folded one level deep and filtered with the page.

title: Graph groups by kind and by test group
description: Folders a record's children by kind only when it has more than one kind, and draws a Tests folder's test-plan groups as nested group nodes (IDs such as `DM-SHOP/test/acceptance`) taken from the folder model.

title: Named graph trail
description: The trail of visited records: each record's title with its ID in parentheses, each group's name with its parent in its tooltip, cut short with an ellipsis.

title: Children lists that tag kinds only when mixed
description: The record tree behind every list of children (record page, side bar, Other records): a layer's components as its children, and each row's kind named only when the list holds more than one kind. `listTitle` titles each list, and names each row's nested list, by its one kind ("Domain rules", "UC requirements of DM-SHOP-UC01"), or "Children" or "Members" when it holds several kinds.

title: Graph motion
description: The shared motion, read from the stylesheet's `--motion-speed` and `--motion-ease` tokens, with `prefers-reduced-motion` turning it off: `cubicBezier`, `parseDuration` and `parseEase` follow the stylesheet's curve in JS, and `readMotion` gives the duration and easing the graph's camera glides on, as do the Model view's camera and the side bar's Outline.

title: Tab model
description: Pure functions over a tab set, generic over each tab's state so anything that holds tabs can own one (a space today, a pane's editor group later): open (activate a page's tab, or open it in the preview tab or as a lasting tab), keep, close (the right neighbor, else the left; the last tab stays as the preview), activate, cycle, update one tab's state, and read a stored set back, dropping anything malformed.

title: Page tabs, kept per space and in the address
description: `usePageTabs`: the focus page's tab sets, one per space, in session storage under `lathe:tabs`, each tab with its views, pane sizes, wiki scroll and graph settings. On each new address it opens the page in its tab set while rendering, so no frame shows the old tab's state, and it keeps the address naming the active tab: activating, cycling and closing move it. A space's first tab starts from the view, sizes and graph settings last used. The page bar shows the tabs as the tab strip on a wide screen and as the Open pages sheet on a phone.

title: Tab strip
description: The `tablist` at the left of the page bar: one `tab` per open page with its ID in mono and its title (a group's label), the preview's title italic, and a tooltip with both in full; the tab is named by what it shows. Beside each tab, never inside it, sits its close button, for the pointer only and hidden from the accessibility tree, since a tablist holds only tabs. Click activates, double-click keeps, middle-click closes; on the focused strip the arrow keys, Home and End move, Enter or Space activates and Delete closes. It scrolls sideways under the wheel and brings the active tab into view.

title: ERD model
description: What a domain's or an aggregate's ERD draws, as plain data: the boxes (aggregates with their root and entity count, or entities with their root mark and fields; boxes from elsewhere with their owner and color), and the lines with their crow's-foot ends, one per entity relationship link on an aggregate and one per aggregate pair and direction on a domain, with the dashed `relates_to` fallback. On an aggregate, its domain events are flags, with a line from the entity raising each and the aggregates reacting to each as faded context; on a domain, one dashed "reacts to" line runs per aggregate pair and event. Also each line's geometry from box edge to box edge, the drawing of its ends, and the offsets that fan out lines between the same two boxes.

title: ERD layout
description: Lays out an ERD left to right along its lines with ELK's layered algorithm, the diagram's own boxes first in model order, so the same diagram always gets the same picture. With domain events, each box goes in the first layer its lines allow, so an event sits right after the entity raising it.

title: Model view
description: Draws a page's ERD with React Flow: each box (blue or gray, root mark, fields, highlight), each line with its ends, a click or Enter on a box going to it, the hover ring, the fit moving with the shared motion, and the key under the diagram with 🟦 and ⬜ for the colors and a drawing of each line end. Domain events are spark flags, notched on the right (`LA-EXP-DR65`); a "reacts to" line shows its label on hover (on a domain, the event's name, always shown by touch), and the key explains the pill and its lines. Its icon is `app/src/model/ModelIcon.tsx`.

title: Graph camera
description: The camera over the one map. `frameOnMap` frames a focus and the levels the depth shows below it, the parent kept in a strip at the left edge (`LA-EXP-DR59`); `frameMap` frames the whole map; `fitBoxes` frames a trace. `zoomPath` is the smooth zoom and pan between two views (van Wijk and Nuij's, as d3-zoom takes), and `glideDuration` its length on the shared motion. `drawnFor` is the level of detail (`LA-EXP-DR60`): the boxes in view and big enough, each with its label, the bars for children too small, within the drawing budget; `mergeDrawn` joins what a glide passes over, so the keyboard's layer takes it once as the glide starts. Its zoom limits, `MIN_ZOOM` and `MAX_ZOOM`, take in the whole map in a phone's pane and frame the deepest leaf of a large product, and a viewport is kept in doubles, the canvas placing each map point on screen relative to the camera's center (`LA-EXP-DR59`). The same camera serves the Nested and Voronoi layouts (`LA-EXP-DR63`, a Voronoi cell framed and drawn by its bounding box): `frameNested` frames the focus's box, and `drawnNested` draws the boxes in view and big enough, each with its label, a parent before its children.

title: Record rows are one link
description: `RecordLink` with `row` marks a row's main link `row-link`. The record rows and trees, problem rows with a record, coverage gaps, open questions, what a requirement fulfills and the patterns a domain follows each mark their one row link. In `app/src/styles.css`, a record list's rows, problem rows and tree rows are positioned; the link's `::after` stretches over the row and carries its hover tint and focus ring; and one rule lifts every other link, button, input and titled badge in the row above it. A tree item's padding sits on its row, so the stretched link covers all of the row and none of its nested rows.

title: Tap to open on a canvas
description: `useTapToOpen`: on a click from a finger or a pen (or, when the event does not say, on a touch screen) a node is selected first, outlined (its element with its `data-id` takes `is-armed`: the Model view's node, the graph's box in its keyboard layer, which the graph's canvas also draws as selected) and named by `TapCard` at the bottom of the canvas with an Open chip; a second tap or the chip opens it, and a tap on the canvas lets go. The graph and the ERD both use it; a mouse click opens at once.

title: The graph header holds still
description: The graph's header is two fixed lines: the trail of records visited is one line whose earlier items shrink with an ellipsis and which scrolls to the center at its end; the toolbar is one line, with the count as one text right after the depth and trace mode and the filters at its end. The graph tells the host what it connects in a layout effect, so the side bar shows it in the same frame.

title: The ERD key and caption hold still
description: The Model view's caption is one line of one text, cut with an ellipsis. Its key has one height for every ERD (`--erd-key-height`), its line ends in up to three rows, so moving between a domain, an aggregate and an entity never resizes the canvas. The canvas is fitted before its first paint, and observes its size once, acting only on a real change.

title: Pages read from bare IDs
description: `parseSpecRoute`: reads a path as a page. `/` is the products; a lowercase first word is an app page (Checks, the reference, or the shell's Settings); an ID is a record, and with the index a product's or a domain's ID is their overview; an ID and more parts is a group; and any other address is missing, which the shell shows as no such page.

title: Graph tree
description: The graph's tree, built once per index from the one folder model the nav reads: a product's Shared folder, domains and kind groups; a domain's stages, their folders and the folders outside every stage; each folder's records, split into one group per kind when it mixes kinds the nav lists side by side, and kept as one list when it holds containers and then the records outside any; a record's children through one group per kind when they are of several kinds. Every stage, folder and group is a node with its address, label, count, members and owner.

title: Edge hints
description: The chips at a canvas's edges that count the boxes of interest past each edge and follow the camera: `pastEdges` counts them, `panToward` is the half-canvas pan, and `EdgeHintChips` draws the chips. In the graph they count the records the center links to (`LA-EXP-UC03-R12`) through the canvas's own camera, drawn again only when a count changes, a click gliding the nearest of them into view; in the Model view (`LA-EXP-C85`), its faded context boxes, a click panning half a canvas that way with the shared motion.

title: Domain event lookups
description: Pure lookups over the index for domain events, shared by the ERD and the aggregate's wiki page: an aggregate's events, the aggregate an event sits under, an event's `raised_by` links to entities, every `reacts_to` link to it, the aggregates reacting to it and the events an aggregate reacts to, each in ID order.

title: Domain events section
description: `DomainEvents` draws an aggregate's "Domain events" section on its wiki page, after its text: one whole-row link per event that says, in the relations' labels, which entity raises it and how many records react to it. The record content leaves the events out of the aggregate's other children.

title: Domain events in the graph
description: The graph draws a domain event as a flag in the spark colors (`LA-EXP-DR65`), and its `reacts_to` and `raised_by` links in their own line style (`relationStyle` gives them `event`): dashed in spark, with the Links switch on too, labeled with the relations' labels. The events reach their aggregate's "Domain events" group through the graph's tree, by the one-kind rule.

title: ELK in a web worker
description: `elkLayout(graph)`: the one ELK the Model view uses (the graph lays itself out without it, `LA-EXP-C04`). In a browser it runs ELK in a web worker (`elkjs/lib/elk-api.js` with `elk-worker.min.js`), so a layout never blocks the main thread; without workers (the tests, in jsdom) it runs the bundled copy. It loads on the first layout, so the wiki's first load leaves it out. On the dev server it also spares the first Model view the seconds Vite took to serve the 1.6 MB bundled ELK as a module.

title: The side bar's Details
description: A record's or group's facts for the side bar: in the Graph and Model views (or for a selected wiki row) its identity with Open, columns with the required ones linked to the reference, the data file and line with the desktop app's file actions, parent, problems and a compact Traceability; in the Wiki view with nothing selected only the data file and line, the columns of its row and the raw links, plus a product's or domain's parent, children and problems. The graph's part (what it connects) follows in the Graph view.

title: The side bar's Outline
description: The wiki's headings read from the wiki pane as it draws them (and again when it changes), each a row that scrolls there, the one in view marked as the pane scrolls; the graph's records in focus grouped by level; the Model view's boxes, those in focus first. Every list is a long list of whole-row links or buttons.

title: The side bar's History
description: The commits that changed the record's rows, from `GET /api/history` (the client is `app/src/views/history.ts`), the uncommitted change first, twenty at a time with Load more, each with the fields it changed before and after in the diff tokens; a calm hint when there is no git. It reloads with the data.

title: Graph map
description: One map per product (`LA-EXP-DR57`): `graphMap` lays out the tree under one root (`mapRootOf` finds the focus's product) once, as an icicle, and keeps it for that index and root. `layoutTree` walks the tree from its roots, sets each depth column's place and width as fixed fractions of the product's box (`MAP_SIZE`, `ROOT_WIDTH`, `COLUMN_RATIO`, `COLUMN_GAP_SHARE`), and from the roots down splits each parent's height equally among its children, a gap apart (`ROW_GAP_SHARE`), giving each group of siblings one text scale, their column's width over `TEXT_SIZE` (`sizeText`) or the largest at which every sibling's label fits its box (`largestFit`, `LA-EXP-C66`), and each node its centered lines (`LA-EXP-DR58`). The same constants and `sizeText` serve the Nested and Voronoi maps. `parentLine` and `linkEnds` say where a parent line and a cross-link meet their boxes, a parent line meeting each box's shape where `outlineInset` (`LA-EXP-C72`) says its outline is (`LA-EXP-DR61`, `LA-EXP-DR65`).

title: Space index
description: `spaceIndex` builds, once per load and product, the index a space reads: the product's records and those of no product, the links among them, their coverage, and its problems with the workspace's. `useSpaceState` hands the current space's index to the nav, quick find, the focus page (wiki, graph, Model view, side bar), the reference, the Checks page and the desktop Dock badge, so none of them can show another product.

title: Graph label text
description: A box's label as part of the map. `labelLines` says what a box's label reads (its title and its kind and ID line), `marksOf` and `hasMarks` its problem badge; `titleWidth` and `metaWidth` measure a line's width with the text measure the maps are laid out with (`setTextMeasure`, `textMeasure`): the canvas's on the loaded faces (`LA-EXP-C82`), or `PLAIN_MEASURE` where there is no canvas (the unit tests). `wrapText` breaks a text into lines on whole words, `wrapLabel` and `linesIn` break a label for a box's width at text scale 1 (a box `w` wide at scale `s` wraps at `w / s`), keeping its kind's shape's room in the Tree (`LA-EXP-DR65`) and its marks' and badge's room, and `labelHeight` is how tall its lines (and its shape's room) need a box to be. `treeLabel` reads a node's label for the Tree map and a trace, `mapLabel` for the Nested and Voronoi maps (with room for its shape's mark), and `labelFor` caches a trace box's lines per measure. `narrowestWidth` is the narrowest box a label fits without breaking a word, and `largestFit` the largest text scale, at most a box's size share, at which a label fits a room (`LA-EXP-DR58`). Every drawn box shows its label (`LA-EXP-DR60`).

title: Graph nested map
description: The Nested map (`LA-EXP-DR62`): `nestedMap` lays out the whole tree of an index once, from one product's root as the Tree map has it (`mapRootOf`), and keeps it for that index. `layoutNested` works from the product's fixed square down: for each group of siblings it sets one text scale, their side's share (`sizeText`) or the largest at which every sibling's label fits (`largestFit`: a leaf's in its square, a parent's in a header band at most `HEADER_SHARE` of it), and one header band, the tallest of their labels; then it lays each parent's children out below its header, inside its padding, as a grid of equal squares in the tree's order (`gridOf`, the column count that makes them largest). Its nodes are the Tree map's (`PlacedMap`), with a header band's height and the tree's order added, so the camera, the minimap and the filters read both maps alike.

title: Graph Voronoi map
description: The Voronoi map (`LA-EXP-DR64`). `voronoiTree` reads a product's tree and labels from an index, with a key that changes only when they do; `layoutVoronoi` makes the product a hexagon of a fixed area (`PRODUCT_AREA`), and from the root down, a group of siblings at a time, gives them one text scale (`shareLabels`: the largest, at most the smallest sibling's size share, `cellText`, at which every sibling's label is placed, a leaf's at its largest inscribed point and a parent's in a header at its top), then splits each parent's room below its header into equal-area cells for its children with `voronoiCells`, a power diagram from the d3-voronoi-map library, seeded deterministically and laid out in the parent's own frame. Convex-polygon helpers (`inset`, `below`, `chord`, `contains`, `holds`) do the clipping. `voronoiMap` lays a product out in the worker (`LA-EXP-C69`) the first time an index asks and keeps it for that index; `readyVoronoiMap` reads it when it is ready, reuses the map of a spec loaded again with the same tree, and lays out on the spot where there is no worker. Its nodes are the Tree map's (`PlacedMap`) with each cell's outline, label box, header cut and the tree's order added, so the camera, the minimap and the filters read all three maps alike.

title: Voronoi layout worker
description: The web worker the Voronoi map is laid out in: it takes a product's tree as `voronoiTree` reads it and sends back the map `layoutTreeOf` makes, so the few hundred milliseconds a large product's power diagrams take never block the page.

title: API and integration sections
description: `ApiSections` lists an API's endpoints and its shared requirements, and `IntegrationSections` an integration's exchanges with its system, each as a tree of rows; `RecordContent` shows them on those kinds' pages in place of the plain list of children.

title: Groups of requirements and rules
description: Pure logic: sorts records into their `group_name`, the ungrouped ones first, then each group in the order it first appears, compared trimmed and in any letter case and headed as first written. The `Grouped` part in parts.tsx draws each group as a part of the page under its heading, which the Outline then lists.

title: Graph shapes
description: Each kind's shape (`LA-EXP-DR65`). `shapeOf` gives a kind's shape and mark (a group's folder, a plain box for a kind it does not know), `nodeShape` a node's by its ID, and `SHAPES` each shape's name for the key, how the canvas draws it (a polygon, rounded corners, or a box with a drawing inside it) and the room it keeps clear of its label, which `wrapLabel` (`LA-EXP-C66`) keeps when it wraps and sizes a label and the box's plate (`LA-EXP-C81`) pads by. `outlineOf` gives a box's outline for its size and box scale (a polygon's corners in map units, or its corner radii), and `notchOf` the notch a drawing inside lines up with; `outlineInset` is where the outline crosses a height, so a parent line meets it (`parentLine`, `LA-EXP-C64`). `shape-icons.tsx` holds each shape's and mark's small drawing, which the canvas draws before a Nested or Voronoi box's kind and ID line and the key shows.

title: Graph painter
description: Draws one frame of the graph on its canvas, in screen pixels at the screen's pixel ratio: the dots behind the map, bars, parent lines and links (dashed curves with their arrows), then each box on screen (its fill, its edge or ring for the focus, the hover, the keyboard's focus ring and a tap's selection, its shape's drawing inside, its marks, its label's lines at their map size times the zoom, its badges), the links' words, and the vignette cut out at the edges. Every point is placed relative to the camera's center in double precision, with no transform but the pixel ratio. The hover spotlight dims the rest a step, fading on the shared motion. A line under `TEXT_BAR_PX` on screen is drawn as a faint bar. `boxLook` and `boxColors` give a box's look and colors, `lineStroke` a line's.

title: Graph box plates
description: `plateOf` makes a box's plate once per map and node, in map units: its outline (its kind's shape in the Tree view and a trace, a box in the Nested view, its polygon in the Voronoi view), its border and look's roles, and its label placed in it as the map broke it: each line's place, font size (its face's size times the box's text scale) and width, the marks before its kind and ID line, and its problem badges where they sit. Nothing in a plate depends on the camera. `plateName` is a box's accessible name, and `plateTip` its tooltip.

title: Graph text faces and measure
description: The faces the canvas draws the graph's text in, from the theme's body and mono stacks (`readGraphFonts`, `fontFor`), and the measure the maps are laid out with: `pageMeasure` waits for the page's fonts and each face to load, then measures with the canvas's own text metrics, each width read once (`canvasMeasure`). The Voronoi worker gets the same measure (`measureSpec`, `workerMeasure`): the stylesheet's @font-face sources, loaded into the worker's own font set, so its layout is measured exactly as the page's.

title: Graph look
description: The graph's look as the canvas draws it, read from the stylesheet's tokens as the browser computes them (`readLook`): the paper, ink, stage, spark, warning and error colors, the hover ring, the links' color, the spotlight's dimming, the vignette's width and the shared motion's fade, so the canvas follows the theme in light and dark. `useThemeVersion` changes whenever the theme may have: its stylesheet, its `data-theme` and `data-mode`, the system's light or dark, or reduced motion.

title: Graph hit testing
description: Finds the box under the pointer from the map's own outlines in map units (`hitPlate`, `inPlate`): a box's rectangle, a shape's polygon or rounded corners (`inPolygon`), a Voronoi cell's polygon, the last drawn first so a child drawn over its parent is found before it. `onScreen` culls a box wholly past an edge of the pane, through the camera relative to its center.

title: Model view edge hints
description: The Model view's edge hints (`LA-EXP-C56`) over its React Flow canvas: the faded context boxes past each edge counted through React Flow's camera, drawn again only when a count changes, a click panning half a canvas that way with the shared motion.

title: Record actions, form and remove question
description: `Editable` wraps a record's page content with its Edit, Add and Remove actions. Edit and Add show the form generated from the schema in place of the content (typed inputs, the parent and links as pickers, part rows that add and remove, Save and Cancel); Remove shows a question that lists what still references the record. Every change is one write; a refusal shows at the top of the form, which takes focus, and beside each input, and a done change is announced.

title: Record form model
description: Pure logic over the schema description: `formFields` and `fieldOf` (a column's input, by its type and enum), `partForms`, `parentChoices` and `linkForms`/`linkTargets` (only records of the allowed kinds in the same product), `childKinds` and `suggestId` (the next free ID), drafts and `draftProblems` (what the form can see before it writes), `commandsFor` (a draft as one write's commands, each with where it came from in the form) and `referrersOf` (what still names a record).

title: Writes from the app
description: `postWrite` sends one write's commands to `POST /api/write` and reads back the changed rows or the store's refusal, a failed request read as a refusal; the shell provides `write`, which reloads the data after a write that went through. Where no writer is provided, a record is only read.

title: Workspace loader
description: `loadWorkspace(root)`: opens the store, which loads the product's data files and Lathe's check rows into the typed tables with every key and rule, or turns its refusal into `data-refused` errors; fills `file_facts` and `file_mentions` from the files tests and components name; creates the coverage views of `lathe/src/coverage.ts`; runs the checks in position order; and reads coverage per domain and obligation kind: designed, built (the designing component's file exists), proved and planned.

title: Engine and app contract
description: The TypeScript types for `Workspace` and its parts, shared by the engine and the web app. Fields may be added, never renamed or removed.

title: Static server
description: `serve({root, port})` serves the prebuilt app from the package's `dist/app`, routes `/api/*` to the shared API (writes included, through the command layer), falls back to `index.html` for client-side routes, and streams `spec:changed` events from `/api/events` when the product's data folder or Lathe's own changes. No route changes the schema: a migration does. `appDir` can point it at another build of the app (the tests use a temporary one).

title: Side-by-side checks and the kept reference
description: In the workspace loader: Lathe's checks, then the product's, run on four connections to the same in-memory database and their problems are put back in run order; the coverage queries run side by side. `loadWorkspace(root, { timings })` fills `timings` with each phase's time (open, files, checks, coverage, total). `buildReference(root)` keeps its answer while no file in the data folders or the schema changes, by size and modification time.

title: Engine performance script
description: `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf`: loads a copy of this repo's data (the code folders linked, so tests' files resolve) cold three times, then changes one row through the store and reloads five times, and holds the median cold load to 2 s and the median reload to 500 ms. It also measures the reference, and a synthetic product of about 10,000 records (Lathe's data copied six times under the prefixes LB to LG), without a budget. It prints each phase's time; above a one-minute load average of 12 (`PERF_MAX_LOAD`) it judges nothing and exits 3.

title: Spec API
description: Lathe's HTTP API (`handleApi`), shared by `lathe serve`, the desktop shell and the app's Vite dev server: `GET /api/spec` (the schema, every stored table's rows, and the checks' problems and coverage), `POST /api/write` (one write through the store's command layer), `GET /api/history` and `GET /api/reference`. It keeps one store open per product root, opening it afresh when the data files change under it, and runs a root's requests one after another. `watchTargets` names the folders whose changes send `spec:changed`: the product's data folder and Lathe's own.

title: App shell and routing
description: The app's frame: the left menu and the hand-rolled History API routing that picks the page for the current address.

title: Dev API plugin
description: Serves Lathe's API inside the app's Vite dev server by loading `LA-PLT-C06` through Vite, so edits to the engine are picked up without a restart. `GET /api/spec` serves the sample fixture, with `x-lathe-source: fixture` and the reason in `x-lathe-source-reason`, when `LATHE_SPEC_FIXTURE=1` is set or the engine cannot be loaded. It watches the product's data folder and the engine's own data and schema, and sends `spec:changed`.

title: Spec data and live reload
description: Fetches `GET /api/spec`, notes whether it came from the engine or the fixture, fetches it again on `spec:changed` and after a write, builds the index from the typed rows (records with their columns and part rows, and the links both ways), and parses addresses into pages.

title: Remembered choices and narrow screens
description: Reads and writes remembered choices (open views, nav and side bar state, pane sizes, open nav sections) to local or session storage, guarded so the app works when storage is missing; with `app/src/shell/useNarrow.ts`, which follows the under-900-px media query for the phone layout and the coarse-pointer query for touch, and keeps Tab inside a sheet.

title: Keymap
description: The one table of keyboard commands (id, title, group, default keys and, where they differ, the keys off a Mac, context), the platform modifier, chord and sequence matching, the typing guard, the reserved browser keys, the overrides from local storage, the duplicate check and how a binding is shown. It lists the tab commands: Ctrl+K then Enter keeps the tab (Alt+K then Enter off a Mac), Alt+Shift+W closes it, and Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycle.

title: Command dispatcher, palette and shortcuts sheet
description: One window key listener that matches presses against the keymap and runs the handler a mounted component registered for that command (so a command applies only while something on screen handles it), calling preventDefault only then; the waiting hint for sequences; the live region for announcements; and the command palette and shortcuts sheet dialogs.

title: App shell commands
description: The shell around every page: the nav state (rail, sheet, menu button), on a phone the top bar and the quick find sheet (`app/src/shell/MobileBar.tsx`) and the theme-color meta, and the commands that work everywhere (quick open, nav, focus nav, back and forward, F12, Checks, F8, `/`, and the `g` sequences).

title: Tooltip
description: Wraps a control: shows its name and its command's keys after a short hover or at once on keyboard focus, one at a time, closed by leaving, blur, a click or Escape; sets `aria-keyshortcuts` and `aria-describedby` from the keymap.

title: Space keys and aria shortcuts in the keymap
description: The keymap's nine space commands (Alt+1 to Alt+9, listed while a space has them), `ariaKeyShortcuts`, and `formatBinding`, which shows keys as the platform does.

title: Shortcut hints in the palette and the sheet
description: `useShortcutHint` gives any control its keys and `aria-keyshortcuts` from the keymap with overrides; the palette shows each row's keys right-aligned in `<kbd>` with `aria-keyshortcuts`; both the palette and the sheet use the title a handler gives ("Switch to Lathe").

title: Shortcut hints on page controls
description: The view toggles, the side bar toggles and the full-screen buttons (and, in the graph and the side bar, the depth buttons, trace switch and hide button) show their keys, for the current platform, through `Tooltip`.

title: Resize handle
description: The one splitter: a focusable vertical separator that turns a pointer position into a value through its host, clamps it, steps it with the arrow keys, Home and End (toward the panel it sizes), resets it on double-click, and reports a drag below a threshold so the host can fold the panel.

title: Workbench panels and sizes
description: The app shell lays the navigation, a gap and the page out on the shell background, and the focus page lays its panes and the side bar out the same way; each panel is marked `panel` and each gap is a resize handle whose size `usePanelSize` (`app/src/shell/prefs.ts`) keeps, within its limits, in local storage. The stylesheet gives every grid its columns.

title: Theme tokens and files
description: The token table (`tokens.ts`: each settable token, its purpose and how its value is checked), the built-in theme files in `themes/`, and reading, completing and writing the versioned theme file.

title: Theme stylesheet
description: Writes a theme as token values on `:root[data-theme]`, the dark set under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` unless Light is chosen and under `data-mode="dark"`; `apply.ts` puts it in one `<style>` element and the mode on `<html>`, at once.

title: Theme store
description: Keeps the person's themes, the chosen one, the mode and the chosen theme's stylesheet in local storage, dropping stored themes that no longer read.

title: Theme provider
description: Holds the themes, the chosen one and the mode; applies what shows and keeps what is chosen; previews without keeping; duplicates, updates, resets, deletes, imports and exports themes.

title: Theme commands and quick pick
description: Registers Color theme, Light, dark or system, and Open Appearance settings; the quick pick (`QuickPick.tsx`) previews as it is arrowed, keeps on Enter and puts back on Escape.

title: Appearance page and theme editor
description: The mode choice, the themes with their previews, import and export, and the editor for a theme of one's own: colors by purpose with light and dark side by side, fonts, text size, density, radius, gap and motion, rename, reset and delete.

title: Contrast audit
description: WCAG contrast (`contrast.ts`) of each text and control token on what it is drawn on, for a theme in a mode: the editor's warnings and the built-ins' check.

title: Early theme script
description: An inline script in the page's head that reads the chosen theme's stylesheet and the mode from storage and puts them on the page before the app's module runs.

title: Page bar
description: The one strip across the top of the open panes, one fixed height: the tab strip at its left; the View group (`aria-pressed` icon buttons with their shortcuts), a divider and the side bar toggle at its right. Compact on a phone: the Open pages button with its count, the View switch as segments, and the side bar toggle.

title: Bottom sheet
description: A sheet that rises from the bottom edge to half the screen, with a grab handle: a tap or a drag up takes it to full height, a drag down to half or away (`settle` weighs the distance and the speed of a flick), Escape or a tap on the dimmed page closes it, and Tab stays inside it. It follows the finger while dragged and slides with the shared motion tokens.

title: Phone top bar and quick find sheet
description: `TopBar`: the menu button, the page's title on one line under a link one step up (`pageHeading` works out both from the address), and quick find. `QuickFindSheet`: quick find as a full-screen dialog, its results a list under the box (`QuickFind` with `inline`), closing on a choice or Escape and giving focus back.

title: Theme color
description: Keeps `<meta name="theme-color">` (declared in `app/index.html`) at the theme's `--sheet` color, following the system's light and dark mode, a theme set on the root element and a theme stylesheet in the head.

title: Touch and phone styles
description: The stylesheet's phone and touch rules: the top bar, the compact page bar, the sheets and their motion, the quick find sheet, the full-screen palette, the tap card, 16 px text boxes, the safe areas and `100dvh`; under `(pointer: coarse)` the 44 px targets (`--touch-target`), as the controls themselves or as a `::before` stretched around a small one, the nav rows at 44 px, and the tab close buttons always shown; and the nav rows as in VS Code's explorer.

title: Stability suite
description: Playwright with Chromium only (`app/stability`). It starts the Vite dev server on a free port (never 5199) over a copy of the data, and runs scripted scenarios with one worker. In each step it records every layout shift (a `PerformanceObserver` for `layout-shift`, with the shifts just after input flagged), long animation frames, and the boxes of key elements frame by frame, and fails a step whose unexpected shift passes 0.01 or whose key elements move, jump back or remount. Shifts that only move the nav or the tab strip are reported as deferred until phase 2 of brief 53. It writes `app/stability/results/summary.json`. A shift's source whose node was taken off the page before the shift was reported is placed by its old box: inside an allowed part it is allowed, otherwise it neither explains nor condemns the shift, so how busy the machine is never decides whether a shift counts.

title: Button
description: `Button` with three variants: `ghost` (the default), `primary` and `icon`, the last requiring a `label` for its accessible name.
