It takes an optional leading `icon` and a `danger` flag, defaults `type` to `button`, and renders a real `<a href>` drawn as a button when given `href`. `buttonClass()` gives the same look to a router link (`Link`, `SpecLink`), which a generic component cannot import. Its classes (`button`, `button-ghost`, `button-primary`, `button-danger`, and `icon-button` for the icon variant) are styled once in `app/src/styles.css`, with the hover tint, the shared focus ring, the pressed look of a toggle and a 44 px target on a coarse pointer. It replaces the outlined `.secondary` and the bordered `.tree-bulk` buttons.

title: Performance suite
description: Playwright with Chromium, one worker (`app/perf`, `npm --prefix app run test:perf`). It builds the app for production into a temporary folder, records each chunk's gzipped size and which ones the first load fetches, and serves the build with `lathe serve`'s server over a copy of the specs on a free port (never 5199). It measures main-thread work from Chromium's own task time (read through the DevTools protocol before and after a step), the longest frame (the longest time between two animation frames, and the long animation frames), and the JavaScript heap after a garbage collection, and holds them to the budgets in `app/perf/budgets.ts`. Above a one-minute load average of 12 it prints the numbers but judges none. It writes `app/perf/results/summary.json`, then runs the engine's script (`LA-PLT-C05`).

title: Views loaded on first use
description: The shell loads the theme editor (`app/src/theme/AppearancePage.tsx`) with `React.lazy`, as the focus page does the graph and the Model view, so the wiki's first load fetches no React Flow and no ELK: about 160 KB of JavaScript gzipped, down from 660 KB. While a page's code loads, its place shows "Loading…".

title: History API
description: Finds the data file that holds a record's row from the data by its ID, never from a path in the request, and reads the commits that changed that row with `git log -G` and `git show`, run by `runGit` with argument arrays inside the product root, a five-second limit and a 512 KB cap, with nothing that writes. `api.ts` routes `GET /api/history` to it.

title: Accessibility suite
description: Playwright with Chromium (`app/a11y`), on the stability suite's harness: the Vite dev server on a free port (never 5199) over a copy of the data, one worker. `audit.spec.ts` runs `@axe-core/playwright` at WCAG 2.2 AA on each page and state, at desktop and phone widths, in four looks (Lathe and High contrast, light and dark), with reduced motion so colors are read at rest; each page in each look is one test. `keyboard.spec.ts` walks the keyboard paths, focus order and announcements. It writes `app/a11y/results/summary.json`, the findings grouped by rule, from which `notes/a11y-audit.md` is written.

title: Surfaces, targets and scroll boxes
description: The shared styles and attributes behind the accessibility audit's fixes: a page that is one panel (`.spec-page.panel`) draws `--paper` so text never sits on the shell; record links listed in a traceability cell (`app/src/styles.css`) or in the side bar's Details (`app/src/views/SideBar.css`) are 24 px tall; and a box that scrolls with nothing focusable in it (a code block in a record's text, the reference page's example, the shortcuts sheet's groups, the ERD's key, the graph's trail) takes `tabindex="0"` and a name.

title: Shell main process
description: Opens each folder in its own `BrowserWindow` (context isolation, sandbox, no Node, no spell check, the preload) on the shell color the theme last sent (`chrome.json`), shown with the launch view over it until the page has its specs (`desktop/src/launch.ts`), or the error page when they fail, with no system title bar (`desktop/src/chrome.ts`); keeps its title; applies the chrome colors its own page sends through `setChrome`, once checked; sends links to other origins to the system browser; saves its bounds and full screen as it moves, resizes, enters or leaves full screen and closes, and tells the page about full screen; pops a native Cut, Copy and Paste menu on text, and the record menu a page asks for (`desktop/src/records.ts`); keeps the Dock badge on the focused product's error count (`desktop/src/dock.ts`); and stops its server when it closes or the shell quits (also on SIGINT and SIGTERM). On launch it opens the folder named on the command line or dropped on the Dock icon, else the most recent folder, else Lathe's repo when run from it, else the Open dialog. The app holds a single-instance lock: a second launch, or a folder from Finder or the Dock, goes to the running app (`desktop/src/instance.ts`). Scroll bars are overlay scroll bars, and macOS window restoration is off (`desktop/src/persistence.ts`). The unpacked app sets its Dock icon, with a DEV band in development. With `LATHE_DESKTOP_SMOKE` set it runs the smoke check in `desktop/src/smoke.ts` and quits.

title: Product folders
description: `checkFolder` says whether a folder opens and where its data folder is, or what is missing; `productNames` reads each product's title from `data/product.jsonl` for the window title; `addRecent` and `parseRecent` keep the recent folders list, saved as `recent-folders.json` in the user data folder.

title: Window state
description: Each folder's saved window (`window-state.json` in the user data folder): `saveWindow` records its normal bounds and whether it is maximized or full screen, and `windowFor` places the next window there, centered when that place is off every screen and shrunk to the largest screen.

title: App servers
description: What a window loads. `startServe` imports `serve()` from the built Lathe package (this repo's `lathe/dist`, or the copy packed into the app's resources) and starts it in-process on a free port for the folder; its server-sent events reload pages when records change. `startDev` picks the development source through `LA-PLT-C44`. Each returns a `stop` the window calls.

title: Development source
description: `chooseDevSource` probes `http://localhost:5199/api/spec` and shares that server when it answers for the opened folder (its `x-lathe-root` header, which `LA-PLT-C08` sets); otherwise `startOwnDevServer` runs the app's Vite (`app/node_modules/vite`) on a free port, never 5199, with `LATHE_ROOT` set to the folder, waits for it, and stops it on request. `vite.config.ts` passes `LATHE_ROOT`, or Lathe's repo, to the dev API plugin.

title: Native menus
description: The menu template: the app menu on a Mac with About Lathe and Settings… (CmdOrCtrl+,, which opens `/settings/appearance` through the `openAppearance` command), File with Open Product Folder… (CmdOrCtrl+O), Open Recent, Open Records In (the editor) and Close Window, the Edit role menu, View with the app commands, Tabs (next, previous, keep and close) and the window roles, the Window role menu, and Help with Record Format and Keyboard Shortcuts (and About Lathe off a Mac, with Settings in File). App command items have no accelerator, except Show Next Tab and Show Previous Tab, which own Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab, since a web page never receives them.

title: Menu commands
description: The app commands the menus offer, each with its keymap ID, its menu label and one of its default bindings, and `keyPresses`, which turns a binding into the key events the app's keymap reads.

title: Preload
description: Runs sandboxed and exposes only `window.latheDesktop`: `isDesktop`, `platform`, `onCommand(listener)`, which returns an unsubscribe function, `setChrome({ background, foreground })`, which passes the two values on to the main process to check, `onFullScreen(listener)`, called at once and whenever the window enters or leaves full screen, `setErrorCount(count)` for the Dock badge, and the record actions `revealRecord`, `openRecordInEditor`, `copyRecordId` and `showRecordMenu`, which send only a record ID. Its type is `Window['latheDesktop']` in `app/src/shell/commands.tsx`. A menu choice goes to the app's listeners by command ID; until the app subscribes, the preload presses the command's default keys in the page, so the app's keymap runs it.

title: Development watcher
description: Builds the shell, starts Electron with `LATHE_DESKTOP_DEV=1`, and on any change under `desktop/src` rebuilds and restarts it; a failed build keeps the running shell. Arguments go on to Electron, such as a folder to open.

title: Local build
description: Packs the built Lathe package with `npm pack` and installs it with its production dependencies (DuckDB) into `desktop/build/stage`, which electron-builder copies into the app's resources. electron-builder's settings in `desktop/package.json` name no signing identity, no publishing and the local Electron; its icons are `build/icon.icns`, `build/icon.ico` and `build/icons/` (`LA-PLT-C57`), and the packed app declares folders as documents it views, so Finder and the Dock can hand it a folder.

title: Window chrome
description: The title bar options of a new window per platform (`chromeWindowOptions`): `titleBarStyle: 'hidden'` everywhere, with the traffic lights centered in the 38 px bar on macOS and a `titleBarOverlay` in the shell's colors on Windows and Linux. `parseChrome` checks what a page sends through `setChrome`, and `applyChrome` sets the window's background and, off a Mac, the controls' overlay.

title: Desktop title bar
description: The app's own title bar, mounted at the top of the app shell (`app/src/App.tsx`) only when `window.latheDesktop` is present, with its styles in `DesktopTitleBar.css`: back and forward (disabled at the history's ends, from the Navigation API), the command center showing the page's heading and opening quick find, and the navigation and side bar toggles, which read from the page whether each panel shows. The bar is a drag region and its buttons are not; it leaves room for the traffic lights on macOS (none in full screen, where they hide) and for the window controls elsewhere (`env(titlebar-area-*)`, else a constant). It also mounts the desktop record hooks with the product's specs.

title: Theme to window chrome
description: The app's view of `window.latheDesktop` (`desktopBridge`), and `useDesktopChrome`, which the theme provider calls: it turns the shown theme's `--shell` and `--ink`, in the shown mode, into opaque `#rrggbb` colors and sends them through `setChrome` whenever they change, following the system's appearance while the mode is System.

title: Dock
description: The Dock's badge text for an error count (`badgeText`, `badgeFor` the focused or last focused window), the check of a count from the page (`parseErrorCount`), and the Dock menu (`dockMenuTemplate`: New Window). The main process sets them with `app.dock.setBadge` and `app.dock.setMenu`, and adds each folder opened with `app.addRecentDocument`.

title: Single instance
description: Where a second launch (`second-instance`, after `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`) and a folder from Finder or the Dock (`open-file`) go: open or focus that folder's window, or bring the app forward. The packed app declares folders as documents it views, so Finder and the Dock hand them over.

title: Launch view and error page
description: The models of the shell's own pages: the launch view and the error page (`static/launch.html`), drawn over a window's app page in a `WebContentsView` until the page's `data-specs` says ready or error, and the About window (`static/about.html`). The main process shows the launch view at once, in the last theme's shell color (`chrome.json`), lifts it when the specs answer, and shows the error page with the engine's message when they fail. `parseLocalAction` lets a page run only the buttons it shows.

title: Local page preload
description: The preload of the shell's own pages: it exposes only `window.latheLocal.act(action)`, which sends a button's action to the main process.

title: App icon
description: Renders `build/icon.svg` (the chuck from `brand/chuck.svg` on a plate on Apple's grid, lit from above) and `build/icon-small.svg` (the same, bolder, for 16 and 32 px) with `rsvg-convert` to `icon.icns` (iconutil), `icon.ico` (ImageMagick), `icons/` for Linux, `icon.png` and `icon-dev.png` (with a DEV band). The outputs are committed; the unpacked app sets its Dock icon from `icon.png`, or `icon-dev.png` in development.

title: Window restoration opt-out
description: Sets `ApplePersistenceIgnoreState` to YES and `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows` to NO in the app's own user defaults before the app is ready, on macOS only; the smoke test writes the same defaults for the unpacked Electron before it launches it.

title: Command layer
description: The store's write path: `add`, `set`, `move`, `link`, `unlink` and `remove`, and `apply` for several as one write, queued so writes run one after another. Each builds the new state in a fresh in-memory database inside one transaction (schema copied, every table inserted in dependency order, the validation queries run), refuses with a `StoreError` that lists every problem with its rule and its file and line or command index, and only then switches to the new state and rewrites the changed tables' files through a temporary file and a rename, sorted by key with columns in the table's order.

title: Merge driver set up for the data files
description: The repo's `.gitattributes` names `**/data/*.jsonl merge=lathe-data`, and the READMEs give the two `git config merge.lathe-data.*` lines each clone runs once, so git merges the data files row by row through `lathe merge-data`.

title: Server contract
description: The shapes the server answers and the app reads, as types only: SpecData for GET /api/spec (the schema description, the data folder, every stored table's rows, the problems and coverage), the WriteRequest and WriteAnswer of POST /api/write (the commands, then the changed rows or the store's problems), and HistoryAnswer for GET /api/history.

title: Coverage queries
description: `COVERAGE_VIEWS_SQL`: views over the typed tables that count coverage from the schema: `obligation_kind` from `meta_kind.obligation`, `role_link` (each design and proof link by `meta_relation.role`, with its source's kind, domain and state and whether its file backs it), `coverage_item` (each obligation a domain owes), and the counts, gaps and tests-by-state queries the engine reads.

title: Unsatisfied check
description: The `unsatisfied` check row: a warning for each obligation in `coverage_item` that no design link targets, of any obligation kind.

title: Unproved check
description: The `unproved` check row: a warning for each obligation in `coverage_item` that no automated or manual test proves, saying when its test is only planned.

title: Coverage assembly
description: `computeCoverage` in the engine builds each domain's `Coverage` from the coverage views: `obligations` in schema order, the tests by state and the gaps. `readRecords` gives each kind its `obligation` and `proof_only` and each relation its `role`, from the schema.

title: Coverage report
description: The coverage part of `lathe check`'s report: one line per domain and obligation kind, such as `LA-CHK requirement: 21/21 designed, 21/21 built, 21/21 proved, 0/21 planned; 0 gaps`.

title: Test file facts
description: `gatherFileFacts` in the engine: for each test with a `file`, records whether the file exists, whether it names the test's ID (or, for a test with a `key`, whether it contains the key), and in the `file_mentions` table which of the test's link targets it names, each matched as a whole ID.

title: Test file missing ID check
description: The `test-file-missing-id` check row: an automated test with a `key` whose file does not contain the key, or an automated test that proves nothing (no `proof`-role link, by `meta_relation.role`) whose file does not name its ID, unless it `supports` a record. A test with a `key_file` is judged by that file, and is left to `test-file-missing` when the key file is missing. A test that proves records but whose file names only some of them is `proof-not-in-file` instead.

title: Test state
description: The `test_state` enum (automated, manual, planned) and the test's `state` column, which every test must give: the store refuses any other value, or none.

title: Test file rules
description: The `test` table's checks that an automated test names a `file` and that a `key_file` comes with a `file`, beside the `test-file-missing` check row, which checks that any test's named file exists whatever its state, and that a `key_file` is a file under the product root.

title: Pattern setting missing check
description: The `pattern-setting-missing` check row: for each use case that follows a pattern, each of the pattern's `pattern_setting` names with no `setting_value` row for that use case and pattern, so a pattern with no settings asks nothing.

title: Setting values per pattern
description: The `setting_value` table: one row per follower, pattern and setting, keyed by all three, with foreign keys to the follower's `follows` link and to the pattern's `pattern_setting` row, so each followed pattern's setting takes its own value; a row gives a value or a not-applicable reason, never both and never neither.

title: Pattern rule coverage
description: The `owed_pattern_rules` view in `COVERAGE_VIEWS_SQL`: each domain that follows a pattern owes each of its rules, unless the domain follows only through use cases and every one of them gives the rule's `setting` a not-applicable reason, or no follower there (a use case, or the domain itself) gives a value that meets the rule's applies-when setting. `coverage_item` reads that view; for a rule owed this way, only design and proof links from records in that domain count, and its gaps carry that domain.

title: Pattern rules in the unsatisfied check
description: The `unsatisfied` check row reads `coverage_item`, so a pattern rule is judged once in each domain that owes it, from that domain's own components, as coverage judges it; while pattern rules need proof only, it reports none.

title: Pattern rules in the unproved check
description: The `unproved` check row reads `coverage_item`, so it warns once for each domain that owes a pattern rule and has no automated or manual test of its own proving it, saying when its only test there is planned.

title: Pattern not followed check
description: The `pattern-not-followed` check row: a warning for each pattern with no `follows` link from a use case or a domain, counting the rules it leaves out of coverage.

title: Obligation outside domain check
description: The `obligation-outside-domain` check row: a warning for each record of an obligation kind that sits in no domain, such as a product's own obligation kind declared under the product, except a pattern rule under a pattern.

title: Pattern rule table
description: The `pattern_rule` table and its kind: under a pattern, an obligation that needs proof only (`meta_kind.obligation` proof), with its `setting` and applies-when setting as foreign keys to its pattern's `pattern_setting` names, and applies-when given whole or not at all. The store refuses a product kind with its name, so it is never widened.

title: Proof not in file check
description: The `proof-not-in-file` check row: for an automated test without a `key` whose file does not name its own ID, one row per `proof`-role link target, by `meta_relation.role`, that `file_mentions` does not list. A `supports` link has no role, so it is never read here; a test with a `key_file` is judged by the key file.

title: Test key fact
description: `gatherFileFacts` in the engine: for a test with a `key`, `contains_id` in `file_facts` says whether the file contains the key text exactly, in place of whether it names the test's ID.

title: Backed proof in the unproved check
description: The `unproved` check row reads `coverage_item`, whose proof comes from `role_link`: an automated test's proof counts only when its file backs it, naming the test's own ID, its key or the target, exactly as coverage counts it.

title: Owed proof count
description: The `planned_any` column of `COVERAGE_COUNTS_SQL`: per domain and obligation kind, the obligations a 'proof' link from a planned source targets, proved or not. For a pattern rule only sources in the owing domain count, as for `planned`.

title: Tests by state query
description: `COVERAGE_TESTS_SQL`: one row per domain with its test records counted by state. `computeCoverage` in `lathe/src/index.ts` puts the row on each domain's `Coverage.tests`.

title: Owed proof and tests in the coverage report
description: The coverage part of `lathe check`'s report adds `; N/T with a planned test` to an obligation line where `planned_any` differs from `planned`, and prints a `<domain> tests: A automated, M manual, P planned` line for each domain.

title: Obligation value reader
description: `readRecords` in the engine gives each kind `obligation` (not `none`) and `proof_only` (`proof`) from `meta_kind.obligation`, which the `obligation_kind` enum keeps to full, proof or none, for Lathe's kinds and a product's alike.

title: Domain-level follows in coverage
description: The followers step of the `owed_pattern_rules` view: a domain record that `follows` a pattern is one of its followers in that domain, beside the use cases that follow it. It owes every rule of the pattern that not applicable cannot take away from it, and its own setting values count towards each rule's applies-when setting; a rule owed both ways is counted once.

title: Proof-only coverage
description: `obligation_kind` carries each obligation kind's `proof_only` into `coverage_item`, so that a proof-only obligation counts as designed and built and has no `satisfies` gap, while its proof is counted as for any other.

title: Proof-only and domain follows in the unsatisfied check
description: The `unsatisfied` check row reads `coverage_item`, which counts a proof-only obligation as designed and finds the domains that owe each pattern rule, itself or through its use cases, so it never reports what coverage does not.

title: Domain follows in the unproved check
description: The `unproved` check row reads `coverage_item`, which finds the domains that owe each pattern rule, a domain that follows the pattern itself included, and warns once for each one with no automated or manual test of its own proving it.

title: Use case without requirements check
description: The `use-case-without-requirements` check row: a warning for a use case with no requirements, skipping a use case that follows a pattern.

title: Pattern rules inside a flow
description: The `flow-step-fulfills-outside-flow` check row adds to a flow's reach the rules of the patterns its use cases or its domain follow, and the interaction requirements that fulfill them, and compares steps' `fulfills` links to pattern rules too.

title: Domain follows and pattern-rule fulfills relations
description: The `follows` table, whose source is the `follows_source` supertype (a domain or a use case), and `fulfills` from an interaction requirement and from a flow step to a pattern rule through the `fulfills_source` and `obligation` supertypes, neither with a role; and `supports` from a test to an obligation, with no role, so it is never design or proof.

title: Proof still owed check
description: The `proof-still-owed` check row: for each obligation a domain owes, judged by the coverage views, that a backed automated or manual proof proves, one row for each planned test also meant to prove it. For a pattern rule only the owing domain's tests count, on both sides.

title: Proof counts nowhere check
description: The `proof-counts-nowhere` check row: each test's proof links, each judged as counting or not by the domains that owe the target, with a reason for each target that does not count. A test is reported when none counts.

title: Manual test file silent check
description: The `manual-test-file-silent` check row: a manual test whose `file` exists, from `file_facts` and `file_mentions`, where the file names neither the test's ID, its key, nor any target of its proof links.

title: Key file facts
description: `gatherFileFacts` reads a test's `key_file`: whether it sits under the root and exists, kept in `file_facts` as `key_file`, `key_file_inside` and `key_file_exists`. When it is named, `contains_id` and the test's `file_mentions` are read from the key file instead of `file`; a missing key file contains nothing.

title: Coverage displays and the product summary
description: The coverage bars (designed, built and proved) on each domain card, and the product's Summary: `ProductSummary` totals coverage, tests, open questions, errors and warnings over the product's domains.

title: Coverage by obligation kind
description: `obligationGroups` turns a domain's coverage into one group per obligation kind from `Coverage.obligations`, in the engine's order. `CoverageBars` draws each group (designed, built, proved, and planned with a hatched bar that is never drawn full), and the product's Summary totals them, with planned on its own line.

title: Shared spec parts and the test state tag
description: The pieces every spec page shares: record links, problem lists, sections and headers. `SpecLink` sends a plain click to the host's `onNavigate` when one is given (through a React context) and to the app's router otherwise. `testState` reads a test's state and `TestStateTag` shows it, dashed and italic for a planned test, with a title saying whether it counts as proof.

title: Patterns, rules and their status per domain
description: Pure logic: a pattern's settings and rules, the use cases and domains that follow it, the patterns a domain follows, a follower's setting values and not-applicable reasons, a rule's applies-when setting and whether a follower's value meets it, and a rule's status in one domain (not applicable with its reasons, waived with the values given, or the components that design and build it and the tests that prove it or are planned to), using the schema's design and proof roles.

title: Patterns we follow, pattern and pattern rule pages
description: The marks for a rule in a domain (designed, built, proved, planned, not applicable with each use case and reason, or "Waived here" with the value given), and what each rule applies when; the domain page's folded list of followed patterns and their rules; the pattern page's settings table, rules under their groups and per-domain tables of following use cases and rule status; and the pattern rule page's list of domains that owe it.

title: Domain page: Patterns we follow and pattern rule coverage
description: The domain wiki's "Patterns we follow" section, filtered by the page's record search, and its Coverage section, which shows every obligation line the engine reports, the `pattern_rule` line among them, and gaps that name each pattern rule.

title: More planned beside the planned bar
description: `obligationGroups` reads `planned_any` into each group's `plannedAny`; `morePlanned` is the difference from `planned`, and `MorePlanned` draws `N more planned` inside the planned bar's row, after its value.

title: Tests by state line
description: `TestCountsLine` draws `Coverage.tests` under `CoverageBars` on the product's domain cards and the domain page.

title: Summary: tests and owed proof
description: The product Summary's `Tests` row, summed over the product's domains by `sumTestCounts`, and the `; N more planned beside proof` note on its `Planned` row.

title: Traceability section
description: `Traceability` draws a record's Traceability section from `traceOf`: the gap callouts (one line per owing domain for a pattern rule), each linked to its check's page; a use case's requirement table, one body per group headed by its name; and each group as a titled list of whole-row links (LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05) that names kinds only when the list mixes them, marks designing components built or not built, and shows a test's file with its state. Long lists stay at ten rows with search.

title: Traceability logic
description: `traceOf` groups a record's links by their labels in the order its kind calls for (an obligation's design, proof and support roles first and its links out last; a component's designs and the tests proving them; a test's proofs and file), and `judge` reads an obligation's standing in a domain from coverage's gaps and the `component-file-missing` check, so the callouts never disagree with coverage. `owingDomains` finds the domains owing a pattern rule. Pure logic, tested directly.

title: Relation labels
description: `linkLabel` names one link by its relation rule's `forward_label` or `reverse_label`, matched by the link's source and target kinds; `relationLabelOf` names a relation by its code alone, for legends; `groupByLabel` groups a record's links by those words. The record facts and side bar, the graph's edges, legend and connections, and the Model view's line titles all read them here.
